clues.name: Monarch
clues.fact: Eastern monarchs fly thousands of miles south to Florida and Mexico each fall, and it takes several generations to return north in spring.

clues.name: White-tailed Deer
clues.fact: Bambi is a roe deer in the original novel, but Disney's 1942 film made him a white-tailed deer.

clues.name: North American Green Frog
clues.fact: Males announce themselves with a call that sounds like a plucked loose banjo string, usually given as a single note.

clues.name: Northern Acorn Barnacle
clues.fact: Its larvae can survive weeks embedded in sea ice and only attach themselves once they've found another barnacle of their own kind.

clues.name: Common Tortoiseshell Limpet
clues.fact: Look for its low, brown-and-white banded shell on stones and boulders crusted with red algae such as Lithothamnion.

clues.name: Jonah Crab
clues.fact: Fishermen once threw it back as a pest that stole bait from lobster traps, but US landings topped 17 million pounds in 2014.

rounds.name: Grand Canyon National Park
rounds.official: Grand Canyon National Park, US, AZ

clues.name: American Robin
clues.fact: With an estimated 370 million birds, it's the most abundant landbird in North America, ahead of red-winged blackbirds and starlings.

clues.name: Mule Deer
clues.fact: Named for its big, mule-like ears, it's often seen stotting, with all four feet coming down together.

clues.name: Gopher Snake
clues.fact: When threatened it puffs up, coils like a rattlesnake and vibrates its tail, but it often strikes with its mouth closed.

clues.name: Common Side-blotched Lizard
clues.fact: In its rock-paper-scissors mating game, yellow-throated males mimic females to sneak matings from the harems of big orange-throated males.

clues.name: Plateau Fence Lizard
clues.fact: A long metallic blue patch runs along each side of its belly, with another on each side of its throat.

clues.name: Uinta Chipmunk
clues.fact: From a rock outcrop or high branch, it can keep up bursts of sharp chip calls for as long as 15 minutes.

clues.name: Great Blue Heron
clues.fact: In South Florida, the Florida Keys and the Caribbean, some are all white, a population known as the great white heron.

clues.name: Spotted Towhee
clues.fact: A big red-eyed sparrow with white-spotted wings, it has a habit of noisily rummaging through dry leaves on the ground for food.

clues.name: Black Phoebe
clues.fact: Always near water, it cements its open cup nest in place with mud under a cliff or a bridge.

clues.name: Desert Spiny Lizard
clues.fact: A frequent tree climber, it favors cottonwoods, yuccas, Joshua trees and ironwood, and is often seen doing territorial push-ups.

clues.name: Plateau Fence Lizard
clues.fact: A long metallic blue patch runs along each side of its belly, with another on each side of its throat.

clues.name: Uinta Chipmunk
clues.fact: From a rock outcrop or high branch, it can keep up bursts of sharp chip calls for as long as 15 minutes.

rounds.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
rounds.official: Rocky Mountain National Park, US, CO

clues.name: Red-winged Blackbird
clues.fact: When researchers dyed males' red shoulder patches black, 64% lost their territories, compared with just 8% of the control birds.

clues.name: Coyote
clues.fact: Coyotes sometimes team up with American badgers to dig out rodents, and some have been seen resting their heads on their badger partners.

clues.name: Yellow-bellied Marmot
clues.fact: Notorious for seeking sweet-smelling radiator fluid, some have ridden out of the Sierra under car hoods to the San Francisco Bay Area.

clues.name: Broad-tailed Hummingbird
clues.fact: Air rushing through two of a male's flight feathers makes a buzzing trill, and in one experiment males without it lost territories more easily.

clues.name: Brown-capped Rosy-Finch
clues.fact: Its bill is yellow in winter and black in summer, and it breeds on mountain peaks in the central Rockies.

clues.name: Wyoming Ground Squirrel
clues.fact: Adults head back underground to hibernate by late July, though the year's young stay above ground as late as September.

clues.name: Song Sparrow
clues.fact: Its fear of hawks and owls seems to be instinctive, but a song sparrow has to learn to be afraid of cats.

clues.name: Convergent Lady Beetle
clues.fact: In the western United States, it may spend up to nine months dormant in large groups in mountain valleys.

clues.name: Pacific chorus frog
clues.fact: Sensing food nearby, it often twitches a toe to lure the prey within easy reach of its tongue.

clues.name: Western Fence Lizard
clues.fact: Ticks carrying Lyme disease that feed on it come away clean, because a protein in its blood kills the bacterium in their gut.

clues.name: White-headed Woodpecker
clues.fact: Birds on southern California's mountaintops have longer bills, apparently an adaptation for feeding on the large, spiny cones of Coulter pines.

clues.name: Yosemite Toad
clues.fact: Nicknamed the tiptoeing toad, it has a habit of crossing snowdrifts without letting its belly touch the cold snow.

rounds.name: Channel Islands National Park
rounds.official: Channel Islands National Park, US, CA

clues.name: House Finch
clues.fact: Sold illegally in New York City as 'Hollywood finches,' birds released in the 1940s went on to settle across the eastern United States.

clues.name: Ochre Sea Star
clues.fact: Remove it from a stretch of shore and California mussels take over almost completely, which is why it's called a keystone species.

clues.name: California Quail
clues.fact: Its curving crest is made of six feathers that droop forward, black in males and brown in females.

clues.name: Western Gull
clues.fact: It's been seen stealing milk straight from an elephant seal's teat, and it'll snatch fish right out of a pelican's mouth.

clues.name: California Seahare
clues.fact: Of the two inks it can release, reddish-purple and milky white, the milky one makes predators attack the cloud as if it were food.

clues.name: Island Fox
clues.fact: North America's smallest fox, it probably reached the Channel Islands with the help of early humans around 7,000 years ago.

rounds.name: Death Valley National Park
rounds.official: Death Valley National Park, US, CA

clues.name: Turkey Vulture
clues.fact: Flying low, it can sniff out the gases that dead animals give off in the early stages of decay.

clues.name: American Coot
clues.fact: Parents favor chicks with the brightest orange-tipped plumes, the first known case of parents selecting for showy ornaments in their young.

clues.name: White-crowned Sparrow
clues.fact: During migration it can stay half-awake for up to two weeks, a trick studied for keeping shift workers and truck drivers alert.

clues.name: Anna's Hummingbird
clues.fact: No other hummingbird has a year-round range this far north, and it rides out snow and subfreezing spells in Seattle.

clues.name: Panamint Rattlesnake
clues.fact: Also called the tiger rattlesnake, it gives birth to live young in July and August, each about 25 centimetres long.

clues.name: Death Valley Pupfish
clues.fact: It can withstand water four times saltier than the ocean and anywhere from freezing up to 116°F, conditions that would kill other fish.

clues.name: Dark-eyed Junco
clues.fact: A flock of these juncos is sometimes called a blizzard, which suits a bird whose scientific name means 'winter junco'.

clues.name: Wild Turkey
clues.fact: Pilgrims brought domestic turkeys with them from England, unaware that this larger wild relative was already living in the forests of Massachusetts.

clues.name: Common Eastern Bumble Bee
clues.fact: Hibernating queens can stay underwater for up to a week without drowning, which may help them survive floods before starting new colonies.

clues.name: Common Box Turtle
clues.fact: When it overheats, it smears saliva on its legs and head, and may even urinate on its hind legs to cool off.

clues.name: Brown-hooded Cockroach
clues.fact: Its young hatch eyeless and without the gut microbes that digest wood, so the parents pass those on by feeding them hindgut fluid.

clues.name: Shenandoah Salamander
clues.fact: Found only on the north-facing talus slopes of Hawksbill, The Pinnacles and Stony Man in Shenandoah National Park.

rounds.name: Cape Cod National Seashore
rounds.official: Cape Cod National Seashore, US, MA

clues.name: Osprey
clues.fact: On every continent except Antarctica, it hunts almost nothing but fish, though in South America it's only a nonbreeding migrant.

clues.name: Eastern Cottontail
clues.fact: Originally absent from New England, it was introduced there and now competes with the native New England cottontail.

clues.name: American Herring Gull
clues.fact: To crack clams and mussels, it drops them from a height onto roads or rocks, a habit that seems to be learned.

clues.name: Atlantic Horseshoe Crab
clues.fact: Cape Cod once offered five cents for every dead horseshoe crab turned in, over a mistaken belief that they hurt fisheries.

clues.name: Longfin Inshore Squid
clues.fact: Few live a full year, and females lay their jelly egg capsules in communal masses of hundreds on the seafloor.

clues.name: Yellow-rumped Warbler
clues.fact: It's the only warbler that can digest waxy berries like wax myrtle, so its eastern birds sometimes winter as far north as Newfoundland.

clues.name: Steller's Jay
clues.fact: A noted mimic, it often imitates the calls of red-tailed hawks and ospreys, sending other birds fleeing for cover.

clues.name: Lorquin's Admiral
clues.fact: Fiercely territorial, it will attack anything that strays into its patch, even large birds.

clues.name: Anicia Checkerspot
clues.fact: Plant chemicals eaten as a caterpillar stay in its body, and its red, yellow and black bands warn predators that it tastes bad.

clues.name: Columbia Spotted Frog
clues.fact: Females lay masses of up to 1,300 eggs that swell to softball size and float free instead of clinging to plants.

clues.name: Columbian Ground Squirrel
clues.fact: Nicknamed 'seven sleepers' for their long hibernation, they greet each other by touching mouths and noses, which looks a lot like kissing.

rounds.name: Point Pelee National Park
rounds.official: Point Pelee National Park, CA, ON

clues.name: Red-tailed Hawk
clues.fact: TV shows often use its rasping scream as a generic raptor sound, even when the bird on screen isn't a red-tailed hawk.

clues.name: Canada Goose
clues.fact: A common park bird, it's often called a pest for its droppings, noise, aggression and habit of stalking and begging for food.

clues.name: Eastern Gray Squirrel
clues.fact: If it feels watched, it fakes burying its food, keeping the morsel in its mouth while covering up an empty hole.

clues.name: Flamed Tigersnail
clues.fact: Its slime is usually orange or reddish, and these snails often burrow and hibernate together in groups over winter.

clues.name: Eastern Comma
clues.fact: This butterfly seldom visits flowers, feeding instead on sap, rotting fruit, dung and minerals it sips from puddles.

clues.name: Eastern Warbling Vireo
clues.fact: The male helps incubate the eggs and may even sing from the nest, a deep cup hung from a branch or shrub.

rounds.name: Pacific Rim National Park
rounds.official: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve, CA, BC

clues.name: Bald Eagle
clues.fact: In 2017 a pair in British Columbia adopted a red-tailed hawk chick they'd likely carried home as prey, and it went on to fledge.

clues.name: California Gull
clues.fact: Utah's state bird, it's remembered for helping Mormon settlers fight a plague of crickets in what's called the Miracle of the Gulls.

clues.name: Giant Green Anemone
clues.fact: Detached mussels seem to be its main food, but in rare cases it has engulfed seabirds, and nobody knows if they were alive.

clues.name: Aggregating Anemone
clues.fact: Rival clone colonies fight with special stinging tentacles, and a scout polyp that comes home badly stung may be attacked by its own clonemates.

clues.name: Pacific Banana Slug
clues.fact: Though it tends to avoid slime trails, even its own, it can find its way back to the same spot after long periods away.

rounds.name: Isle Royale
rounds.official: Isle Royale National Park, US, MI

clues.name: Cedar Waxwing
clues.fact: If only one bird at a time can reach a twig's berries, a flock may line up and pass them beak to beak.

clues.name: American Toad
clues.fact: Fish have reportedly died after eating just one of its toxic tadpoles, but most fish quickly learn to leave them alone.

clues.name: Chalk-fronted Corporal
clues.fact: Unusually sociable for a dragonfly, it often perches in groups and readily approaches people to eat the mosquitoes and biting flies they attract.

clues.name: Trumpeter Swan
clues.fact: With fewer than 70 known in the wild in 1933, extinction looked close until aerial surveys found thousands around Alaska's Copper River.

clues.name: Boreal Snaketail
clues.fact: Rated secure worldwide, it's critically imperiled in New York, with pollution and dammed waterways among its main threats.

clues.name: Diervilla Clearwing
clues.fact: Its caterpillars' only known host plant is northern bush honeysuckle, so this bumblebee mimic's range is limited by where the honeysuckle grows.

clues.name: American Crow
clues.fact: Crows have been seen robbing a river otter, one pecking its tail as a distraction while the others swooped in and stole its fish.

clues.name: Northern Cardinal
clues.fact: Defending his territory, a male may mistake his reflection in a shiny surface for an invading rival and fight it relentlessly.

clues.name: Green Anole
clues.fact: Its ancestors crossed the sea from Cuba to the southern United States, a rare case of an island lizard colonizing a mainland.

clues.name: American Alligator
clues.fact: When water starts to freeze, it pokes its snout through the surface to breathe above the ice and can stay that way for days.

clues.name: Florida Woods Cockroach
clues.fact: When alarmed, adults can shoot a foul-smelling spray up to a meter, which is why it's also called the Florida skunk roach.

clues.name: Pygmy Rattlesnake
clues.fact: North America's smallest rattlesnake has a rattle so tiny that its buzz can only be heard from a few feet away.

rounds.name: Santa Ana Wildlife Refuge
rounds.official: Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge, TX, US

clues.name: Pond Slider
clues.fact: The 'slider' in its name comes from how basking groups scramble off logs and shoot back into the water when they sense danger.

clues.name: Gulf Fritillary
clues.fact: Its species name, vanillae, comes from a 1705 painting showing it on a vanilla orchid, a plant its caterpillars don't actually use.

clues.name: White-winged Dove
clues.fact: North America's only game bird that's also a migratory pollinator, it leans heavily on saguaro nectar and fruit where the cactus grows.

clues.name: Common Spotted Whiptail
clues.fact: Its tail is usually close to three times the length of its body, and males often show a red throat and blue belly.

clues.name: Brown Longtail
clues.fact: Its caterpillars feed on grasses, including Bermuda grass and Johnson grass, and southern Texas sees three generations a year.

rounds.name: Padre Island
rounds.official: Padre Island National Seashore, US, TX

clues.name: Common Raccoon
clues.fact: To climb down a tree headfirst, an unusual skill for a mammal its size, it rotates its hind feet so they point backwards.

clues.name: Great-tailed Grackle
clues.fact: The Aztecs brought it to Tenochtitlan around 1500, probably for its iridescent feathers, and that's the earliest documented bird introduction in the Americas.

clues.name: Salt Marsh Moth
clues.fact: Plant toxins called pyrrolizidine alkaloids don't seem to bother it, and it can detoxify them and even turn them into sex pheromones.

clues.name: Western Ribbon Snake
clues.fact: A whitish, unmarked upper lip stands out against the dark head, and the very long tail makes up about a third of its length.

clues.name: Texas Glowing Click Beetle
clues.fact: Its light comes from glowing spots on each side of its thorax and a small light organ on its abdomen.

clues.name: Keeled Earless Lizard
clues.fact: Named for the keeled scales on its back, it's perhaps most common in the loose, shifting sands of beaches and barrier islands.

clues.name: Malachite
clues.fact: Adults feed on nectar, rotting fruit, dead animals and bat dung, and the green chrysalis has sharp gold spines that can puncture predators.

clues.name: Social Flycatcher
clues.fact: It often nests near bee or wasp nests, building a bulky domed cup that can include cotton, paper and other human-made fibers.

clues.name: Giant Toad
clues.fact: Rhinella, the first word of its scientific name, means 'little nose', built from the Greek for nose and a Latin ending for small.

clues.name: Tiger Longwing
clues.fact: Like other longwings, its caterpillars eat passion flower vines, and its bright wing pattern warns predators that it tastes bad.

clues.name: Mantled Howler Monkey
clues.fact: Disturb one and it'll often show its irritation by urinating or defecating on you, with good aim from high in the trees.

clues.name: Green-crowned Brilliant
clues.fact: Instead of hovering, it usually clings to a flower to feed, and males sometimes defend patches of Marcgravia vines, a main nectar source.

clues.name: Black Vulture
clues.fact: Sharp eyes help it find carcasses, and so does tailing other vultures that have a keen sense of smell.

clues.name: Black Spiny-tailed Iguana
clues.fact: The Guinness Book of World Records lists it as the world's fastest lizard, with a top sprint speed of 34.6 kilometers per hour.

clues.name: Central American Agouti
clues.fact: Agoutis placed fourth for sense of smell in an analysis of 240 species, beating dogs, which came out only average.

clues.name: Brown-throated Three-toed Sloth
clues.fact: Algae grow in tiny cracks in its coarse hairs, sometimes giving it a greenish tint, and its neck can turn up to 270 degrees.

clues.name: Central American White-faced Capuchin
clues.fact: On Jicarón Island, male capuchins took up a fad of kidnapping baby howler monkeys and carrying them around on their backs.

clues.name: Many-scaled Anole
clues.fact: Found only around Costa Rica's Golfo Dulce, it bobs its head and flashes an orange-yellow throat fan to attract mates and mark territory.

rounds.name: Sian Ka'an
rounds.official: Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve, QR, MX

clues.name: Double-crested Cormorant
clues.fact: The auritum in its scientific name comes from the Latin for 'eared', after the same breeding crests above its eyes that make it double-crested.

clues.name: Brown Anole
clues.fact: In the US it has pushed the native green anole up into the treetops, and it sometimes eats green anole hatchlings too.

clues.name: Collared Aracari
clues.fact: As many as seven may share a single cavity to roost overnight, and they usually travel in groups of about six to fifteen.

clues.name: Turquoise-browed Motmot
clues.fact: Known as the clock bird on the Yucatán Peninsula, it swings its racket-tipped tail like a pendulum to tell predators it's spotted them.

clues.name: Yucatan Jay
clues.fact: Juveniles have white heads and bodies that soon molt to black, but their yellow bills take into the second year to turn fully black.

clues.name: Yucatan Vireo
clues.fact: In Belize it sings an evenly paced warble written as 'cheer up sweet' or 'cheer up why not sweet'.

clues.name: Green Heron
clues.fact: Listen for a loud, sudden kyow, and look for a chestnut neck often pulled in tight against the body.

clues.name: Little Blue Heron
clues.fact: Despite the 'blue' in its name, young ones stay almost entirely white, like a snowy egret, until their second year.

clues.name: Northern Jacana
clues.fact: Females are much bigger than males, and each can keep up to four males, who build the floating nests and incubate the eggs.

clues.name: Morelet's Seedeater
clues.fact: Meant to honor the collector Morelet, its scientific name came out misspelled as morelleti, and naming rules say the typo stays.

clues.name: Green-backed Sparrow
clues.fact: Its nest is a dome on the ground with a side entrance, and nobody has yet studied what it eats.

clues.name: Black-throated Shrike-Tanager
clues.fact: Pairs almost always join mixed-species flocks, often acting as sentinels and snatching prey the flock stirs up in fast, acrobatic chases.

clues.name: Saffron Finch
clues.fact: Called the 'roof canary' in northern Venezuela, it usually nests in cavities like old rufous hornero nests or under house roofs.

clues.name: Rufous Hornero
clues.fact: Argentina's national bird sings in duets, each partner beating its wings in time with its trill, so the faster flapper is the male.

clues.name: Argentine Black-and-white Tegu
clues.fact: It's one of the few partly warm-blooded lizards, running up to 10 degrees Celsius warmer than its surroundings at night in breeding season.

clues.name: Plush-crested Jay
clues.fact: Raising chicks is a group effort, with several flock members bringing food and even getting rid of the nestlings' droppings.

clues.name: Western Collared Spiny Lizard
clues.fact: As in all Tropidurus lizards, males and females are marked differently, and the male is usually much larger and more brightly colored.

rounds.name: Tijuca National Park
rounds.official: Parque Nacional da Tijuca, RJ, BR

clues.name: South American Coati
clues.fact: Solitary males were once thought to be a separate species, called coatimundis, because they live so differently from the female bands.

clues.name: Spiny-legged Stingless bee
clues.fact: Unable to sting, it defends the nest by tangling itself in a person's hair, buzzing loudly and crawling into their ears and nose.

clues.name: African Hermit Spider
clues.fact: This African spider has a foothold in Brazil, Colombia and Paraguay too, probably brought over by people in the late 1800s or earlier.

clues.name: Rock River Frog
clues.fact: This rock-loving frog can even live on rocky sea shores, where it forages in the intertidal zone.

clues.name: Santa Catarina Tree Toad
clues.fact: Males measure about 25 to 28 mm from snout to vent, with a brown or gray back marked with stripes and a white belly.

clues.name: Rufous-collared Sparrow
clues.fact: It's been seen picking termites out of spider webs, and its diverse vocalizations have been studied intensely since the 1970s.

clues.name: Sayaca Tanager
clues.fact: It feeds on flowers, buds and insects, a mixed diet that's helped make it one of the most common city birds in southeastern Brazil.

clues.name: White-eyed Parakeet
clues.fact: Its species name, leucophthalmus, means 'white eye' in Greek, but the eye itself is orange, ringed by bare white skin.

clues.name: Masked Water-Tyrant
clues.fact: Its range is split in two: eastern and southern Brazil, and a far-off area from southwestern Colombia through western Ecuador into Peru.

clues.name: Green-headed Tanager
clues.fact: Its flashy blue-green colors camouflage it well among the leaves, so it's easy to miss even in the orchards and parks where it's common.

clues.name: Itatiaia Spinetail
clues.fact: Named for the Serra do Itatiaia, it usually lives above the tree line, from 1,850 to 2,800 meters up.
clues.by: Rob Van Epps, bazı hakları saklıdır (CC BY-NC), yükleyen: Rob Van Epps

clues.name: Great Kiskadee
clues.fact: Brazilians know it as bem-te-vi, 'I saw you well,' an echo of its exuberant BEE-tee-WEE call.

clues.name: Blue-gray Tanager
clues.fact: It's more common in forest growing back on abandoned slash-and-burn plots than in primary forest that's never been cleared.

clues.name: South American Common Toad
clues.fact: Once thought to be one species, this toad is really a complex of 16 named species, with others still waiting to be recognized.

clues.name: Black Agouti
clues.fact: Apart from its main range in the northwestern Amazon, there's a separate population in the Magdalena River valley of northern Colombia.

clues.name: Ecuadorian Squirrel Monkey
clues.fact: At 34 to 44 cm, its tail is longer than its head and body put together.

clues.name: Ecuador Poison Frog
clues.fact: Males sing from slightly raised spots to find a female, and the frog's Latin name, bilinguis, comes from its two-pulsed call.

clues.name: Southern Lapwing
clues.fact: South America's only crested wader, it has red bony spurs on its wings to intimidate foes and fight birds of prey.

clues.name: Capybara
clues.fact: Its meat is popular in Venezuela during Lent, since legend has it the Catholic Church once allowed it while other meats were forbidden.

clues.name: Giant Otter
clues.fact: Known in Brazil as the water jaguar, it's the noisiest otter, and each family has its own audio signature.

clues.name: Yacare Caiman
clues.fact: Some teeth in its lower jaw poke through holes in its upper jaw, which earned it the name 'piranha caiman'.

clues.name: Hyacinth Macaw
clues.fact: Its beak can crack coconuts, yet acuri palm nuts are so hard that it only eats them once they've passed through cattle.

clues.name: Chestnut-bellied Guan
clues.fact: Found only in Brazil, this guan has a rough, crowlike song and white spots running from its chest to its belly.

rounds.name: Península Valdés
rounds.official: Península Valdés World Heritage Site, AR

clues.name: Subtropical Lady
clues.fact: Also called the western painted lady, it ranges from the mountains of Colombia down to Patagonia, and is even found on Easter Island.

clues.name: South American Sea Lion
clues.fact: At Península Valdés, orcas will beach themselves to grab these sea lions near the shore.

clues.name: Magellanic Penguin
clues.fact: Each year the male reclaims last year's burrow and waits for his partner, who can recognize him by his call alone.

clues.name: Elegant Crested-Tinamou
clues.fact: Its flights cover only about 500 meters, and a botched takeoff can end in a fatal crash into a branch or wire.

rounds.name: The New Forest
rounds.official: The New Forest National Park, Hampshire, England, England, GB

clues.name: Great Spotted Woodpecker
clues.fact: As late as the early 1900s some thought its drumming might be vocal, and it wasn't proved purely mechanical until 1943.

clues.name: Eurasian Blackbird
clues.fact: Its name dates from when 'bird' meant a small bird and crows were 'fowl,' making it the only common black 'bird' in the British Isles.

clues.name: European Robin
clues.fact: Territorial fights cause up to 10% of adult robin deaths in some areas, and robins have even been recorded attacking their own reflection.

clues.name: Common Field Grasshopper
clues.fact: An interested female answers a male's song with a similar one, and the two can trade songs until they mate or she loses interest.

clues.name: Brimstone Moth
clues.fact: Its bright yellow wings, with small brown patches along the front edge of each forewing, make it unmistakable in its range.

clues.name: Gatekeeper
clues.fact: To tell it from the meadow brown, look for wings held open at rest and double pupils in the eyespots.

rounds.name: The Lake District
rounds.official: Lake District National Park, England, GB

clues.name: Common Chaffinch
clues.fact: After farmers thresh their crops, it sometimes spends weeks picking grain out of the discarded chaff, which likely gave it its name.

clues.name: Black-headed Gull
clues.fact: Mostly a bird of Europe and Asia, it also breeds in small numbers on the coast of eastern Canada.

clues.name: Common Darter
clues.fact: One of the easiest dragonflies to photograph, it keeps coming back to the same sunny perch, so you can predict where it'll land.

clues.name: Cinnabar moth
clues.fact: Its caterpillars eat ragwort so greedily that big groups can strip whole patches bare, and when food runs short they may turn cannibal.

clues.name: Dark Giant Horse Fly
clues.fact: Europe's heaviest fly comes with a very loud buzz, but it usually takes blood only from cows and horses and avoids people.

clues.name: European Minnow
clues.fact: An injured minnow releases Schreckstoff, German for 'fear substance', from its skin, and the rest of the shoal bunches tighter together.

rounds.name: Picos de Europa
rounds.official: Parque Nacional de los Picos de Europa

clues.name: Common Blue
clues.fact: Females are usually brown, but colder temperatures while they develop make them bluer, and in Ireland and Scotland their upperwings can be mostly blue.

clues.name: Common Buzzard
clues.fact: Described as 'sluggish and not very bold', a resident buzzard can spend more than half its day just sitting on a perch.

clues.name: Eurasian Griffon
clues.fact: In soaring flight it burns only about 1.43 times its resting metabolic rate, compared with upwards of 16 times for other birds.

clues.name: Ocellated Lizard
clues.fact: One of the biggest wall lizards, it robs birds' nests for eggs and nestlings and sometimes eats other lizards and small snakes.

clues.name: Podarcis lusitanicus
clues.fact: Look for this lizard in Portugal and Spain, the two countries where it's found.

clues.name: Iberian Rock Lizard
clues.fact: Green spreads over it with age, belly first and then the back, and females tend to mate with the greener males.

rounds.name: The western Canary Islands
rounds.official: Santa Cruz de Tenerife, CN, ES

clues.name: Yellow-legged Gull
clues.fact: When Italy's 2020 lockdown cut off their food scraps, Rome's yellow-legged gulls turned to hunting prey as large as rats and rock doves.

clues.name: Barbary Partridge
clues.fact: It's Gibraltar's national bird and appears on the local penny coins, even though it was introduced there.

clues.name: faya bayberry
clues.fact: Native to the Canaries, Madeira and the Azores, it's invasive in Hawaii, where it crowds out native trees and deeply alters nitrogen cycling.

clues.name: East Atlantic Sally Lightfoot Crab
clues.fact: Hard to catch by day, it tends to freeze when someone shines a flashlight on it at night, which makes it easy to collect.

clues.name: Island Canary
clues.fact: The bird is named after the Canary Islands, and the islands' name comes from the Latin for 'islands of dogs'.

clues.name: Tenerife Lizard
clues.fact: A fruit, flower and nectar eater, it's a major pollinator and seed disperser, and sometimes a nuisance in vineyards and orchards.

clues.name: Speckled Wood
clues.fact: Northern speckled woods are bigger and darker than southern ones, with longer forewings that help them handle cooler temperatures.

clues.name: Iberian Green Frog
clues.fact: The Sahara frog of North Africa is its closest living relative, and the two may have split when the Mediterranean dried up.

clues.name: European chain fern
clues.fact: It's called chain fern for the linked spore clusters under its fronds, and the frond tips grow new plantlets that take root.

clues.name: Berthelot's Pipit
clues.fact: Compared with a meadow pipit, it looks shorter-tailed and bigger-headed, and its 'schrip' call sounds like a yellow wagtail's.

clues.name: Madeira Lizard
clues.fact: Ships trading between Madeira and the Azores accidentally carried it across, and it now lives wild in the Azores too.

clues.name: Northern Wheatear
clues.fact: The name wheatear is an altered, perhaps cleaned-up form of 'white-arse,' after its prominent white rump.

clues.name: Song Thrush
clues.fact: It's the emblem of West Bromwich Albion football club, because the pub the team once changed in kept a pet thrush in a cage.

clues.name: European Common Frog
clues.fact: In the Alps it can stay in hibernation until early June, getting all the oxygen it needs through its skin.

clues.name: Chalkhill Blue
clues.fact: It turns in early, settling for the night with its wings closed on grass stalks or flower tops while it's still full daylight.

clues.name: Yellow-billed Chough
clues.fact: It has nested at 6,500 meters, higher than any other bird, and has been seen following climbers on Mount Everest at 8,200 meters.

clues.name: Swiss Brassy Ringlet
clues.fact: When the ice retreated about 130,000 years ago, its ancestors followed their habitat uphill and were stranded in different mountain ranges, becoming separate species.

rounds.name: Gran Paradiso
rounds.official: Gran paradiso National park opposite ski resorts

clues.name: Whinchat
clues.fact: Singing from fences, bushes and wires, the male often mixes phrases from at least 12 other bird species into his soft, crackly song.

clues.name: Small Tortoiseshell
clues.fact: With its wings shut, it looks like a leaf, and birds may take up to 30 minutes to spot one on the ground.

clues.name: Silver-washed Fritillary
clues.fact: Unusually for a butterfly, the female lays her eggs in tree bark a meter or two up, close to the violets her caterpillars eat.

clues.name: Common Wall Lizard
clues.fact: Cincinnati calls it the Lazarus lizard because a boy whose family owned the Lazarus department stores released about 10 there around 1950.

clues.name: Northern Chamois
clues.fact: Chamois tend to watch for danger from below, so a hunter stalking them from above is less likely to be spotted.

clues.name: Marbled Ringlet
clues.fact: Its name comes from the underside of its hindwings, marbled in chestnut brown with clearly marked whitish veins.

clues.name: European aspen
clues.fact: Flattened leaf stalks make its leaves tremble in even a slight breeze, which is where the scientific name tremula comes from.

clues.name: Viviparous Lizard
clues.fact: No other land reptile lives farther north, and in especially cold winters it can freeze completely and thaw out two months later.

clues.name: European Comma
clues.fact: Its caterpillar wears a white stripe that mimics a bird dropping, and folded up, the adult looks like a dead leaf.

clues.name: Common Slowworm
clues.fact: Possibly the longest-lived lizard, it lives about 30 years in the wild, and one male lived at least 54 years at Copenhagen Zoo.

clues.name: Ash-black Slug
clues.fact: The world's largest land slug can grow past 30 centimeters, but it mostly eats mushrooms and algae and isn't considered a pest.

clues.name: Pine Hawkmoth
clues.fact: Females lay their eggs in twos and threes along pine or spruce needles, which the caterpillars then eat.

clues.name: White Wagtail
clues.fact: The national bird of Latvia, it's adapted to towns by foraging for insects on paved areas like car parks.

clues.name: Hooded Crow
clues.fact: A scarce winter visitor to eastern England from Scandinavia, it picked up local names there like 'Royston crow' and 'Danish crow'.

clues.name: Roman Snail
clues.fact: Eaten by the ancient Romans and prized in French cooking as escargot, it's hard to farm and rarely raised commercially.

clues.name: grass snake
clues.fact: It can rear up and flatten its head and neck like a cobra, a trick that may date from when cobras lived in Europe.

clues.name: European Fire-Bellied Toad
clues.fact: When threatened it lifts its arms, sometimes flipping over, to flash its black-mottled red belly and warn predators it's toxic.

clues.name: Aquatic Warbler
clues.fact: Mainland Europe's rarest passerine, it breeds mostly in the Polesie region of Poland and Belarus, home to 70 percent of the world's population.

clues.name: European Goldfinch
clues.fact: Because it eats thistle seeds, Christian symbolism links it to Christ's crown of thorns, as in Raphael's Madonna of the Goldfinch.

clues.name: Eurasian Kestrel
clues.fact: An old name for it is windhover, from its habit of hovering in the air, and kestrels were once used to keep pigeons away.

clues.name: Sand Lizard
clues.fact: Rematches between rival males tend to be much shorter than their first fight, likely because they recognize each other and can predict the outcome.

clues.name: European Tree Frog
clues.fact: It croaks as rain approaches, so people once used it as a living barometer.

clues.name: European Fire-Bellied Toad
clues.fact: When threatened it lifts its arms, sometimes flipping over, to flash its black-mottled red belly and warn predators it's toxic.

clues.name: Danube Crested Newt
clues.fact: The smallest crested newt, it has a slender swimmer's body built on 16 or 17 rib-bearing vertebrae, more than any other crested newt.

clues.name: Small Copper
clues.fact: Males vigorously defend small territories against rivals or any passing insect, and even a big bird's shadow overhead can set one off.

clues.name: Scarce Swallowtail
clues.fact: It's quite common despite the name, which comes from how rarely it reaches Britain.

clues.name: Roughtail Rock Agama
clues.fact: Its dung was once imported from the Levant to European pharmacies and used as an eye medicine and a cosmetic.

clues.name: Mytilene Bright Bush-Cricket
clues.fact: Bright bush crickets are named for their often bright colors, and their antennae run about three times the length of their body.

clues.name: Old World Swallowtail
clues.fact: Its caterpillar starts out looking like a bird dropping and can push out a smelly orange fork that deters insects but not birds.

clues.name: Chocolate-band Snail
clues.fact: It lies dormant through winter in northern Greece but through summer in Crete, with adults digging into the soil and juveniles sheltering under stones.

clues.name: Middle Eastern Flower Scarab
clues.fact: These day-active chafers often feed on flowers, and each species has its own distinctive pattern, usually white dots or lines on black.

clues.name: Western Caspian Turtle
clues.fact: It will accept bread from people but lacks the enzymes to digest it, so those handouts are bad for its health.

clues.name: Cretan Wall Lizard
clues.fact: You'll only find this wall lizard on Crete and the satellite islands around it, nowhere else in the world.

clues.name: Common Carder Bumble Bee
clues.fact: Queens prefer to build in old mouse nests, shaping moss and grass into a small hollow ball partly bonded with wax.

clues.name: European Edible Sea Urchin
clues.fact: Its name esculentus means edible, but its white gonads, the part that's eaten, make it less prized than urchins with orange ones.

clues.name: Common Moon Jelly
clues.fact: You can spot it by the four horseshoe-shaped gonads showing through the top of its almost entirely translucent bell.

clues.name: Great Skua
clues.fact: It often robs gulls, terns and even northern gannets of their fish, and it'll fly at the head of anyone approaching its nest.
clues.by: Janne Asp, זכויות יוצרים חלקיות (CC BY-NC-ND), הועלה על ידי Janne Asp

clues.name: Lion's Mane Jelly
clues.fact: Detached tentacles can sting for up to 25 days, and in 2010 one broken-up jellyfish is thought to have stung about 150 beachgoers.

clues.name: Swedish Cornel
clues.fact: Its four white 'petals' are really bracts around a tight cluster of small dark purple flowers, and its fruit is a red berry.

clues.name: Green-veined White
clues.fact: Males give off a sex pheromone people can actually smell, citral, the compound that gives lemon peel oil its flavor.

clues.name: Cranberry Blue
clues.fact: True to its name, its caterpillars feed on cranberry and bilberry, and it flies low on very broad, rounded wings.

clues.name: Dwarf Birch
clues.fact: Its bark doesn't peel and is a shiny red-copper, and its small rounded leaves turn red in autumn.

clues.name: Azure Hawker
clues.fact: Basking on stones or tree trunks with its wings lowered, it can warm its body as much as 7 degrees Celsius above the air.

clues.name: Lapland Bumble Bee
clues.fact: Many specimens collected as this taiga and tundra bee turn out to be other bumblebees, so its exact range is still unclear.

clues.name: Bombus balteatus
clues.fact: Its tongue can reach two-thirds of its body length, but in the Rockies it has trended shorter as long-tubed flowers declined.

clues.name: Common Bulbul
clues.fact: Its loud call goes 'doctor-quick doctor-quick be-quick be-quick', and its flight is bouncing and woodpecker-like.

clues.name: Blue Monkey
clues.fact: It often teams up with red-tailed monkeys for extra protection, and the two species even groom each other.

clues.name: Olive Baboon
clues.fact: In Eritrea, olive baboons use water holes dug by elephants, while the elephants use baboons in the treetops as an early warning system.

clues.name: Great Blue Turaco
clues.fact: The Mbuti people of the Ituri Rainforest call it kulkoko and believe it warns okapis of danger by calling loudly.

clues.name: Johnston's Chameleon
clues.fact: Only adult males grow three ringed horns, and they're fiercely territorial, fighting other males with horns and bites.

clues.name: Impala
clues.fact: Seemingly the only hoofed mammal that grooms itself and others, it combs ticks from a partner's head and neck with its lower front teeth.

clues.name: African Wolf
clues.fact: Long mistaken for a golden jackal, it was shown by DNA studies in 2015 to be closer to gray wolves and coyotes.

clues.name: Gray-headed Kingfisher
clues.fact: It guards its nest hole in a steep riverbank by repeatedly dive-bombing foraging monitor lizards.

clues.name: Gray Crowned-Crane
clues.fact: Along with the black crowned crane, it's the only crane that can roost in trees, thanks to a long hind toe that grips branches.

clues.name: Superb Starling
clues.fact: Check the eyes: pale creamy white on this one, red on the look-alike Hildebrandt's starling, which also lacks the white breast band.

clues.name: Taveta Golden-Weaver
clues.fact: Named after Kenya's Taveta region, it breeds in colonies, with males weaving oval nests onto reed or grass stems over water.

clues.name: Common Warthog
clues.fact: It kneels on calloused pads on its wrists to graze, and those pads start forming before it's even born.

clues.name: Tropical Boubou
clues.fact: Its bou, hou and boubou calls give it its name, and pairs duet so fast they sound like one bird.

clues.name: Marabou Stork
clues.fact: Marabous living off garbage dumps will swallow virtually anything, and they've been seen eating shoes and pieces of metal.

clues.name: Grant's Gazelle
clues.fact: Predators are less likely to attack it when it joins a group of Thomson's gazelles, perhaps because the Thomson's make easier targets.

clues.name: Thomson's Gazelle
clues.fact: At a shared border, neighboring males hold mock fights, charging without touching, then grazing their way apart with no winner.

clues.name: Golden-winged Sunbird
clues.fact: Females that stray into a bronzy sunbird's territory may beg by quivering their wings and fanning their tails, and the bronzy lets them feed.

clues.name: Hadada Ibis
clues.fact: Named for its extremely loud haa-haa-haa-de-dah call, often given in flight as birds leave and return to roost trees.

clues.name: African Savanna Elephant
clues.fact: A lower-ranking elephant greets its superior by putting the tip of its trunk into the other's mouth.

clues.name: Dickinson's Kestrel
clues.fact: Also called the white-rumped kestrel, it's mostly dark gray with a pale head and rump, and bare yellow skin around the eye.

clues.name: Collared Palm-Thrush
clues.fact: A black line outlines its throat, and its pale eye and unspotted underparts set it apart from the similar spotted morning-thrush.

clues.name: Puku
clues.fact: When scared, it repeats a shrill whistle, and in the rainy season female herds band together, often around 50 strong, for safety.

clues.name: Lilian's Lovebird
clues.fact: The smallest parrot on mainland Africa, it's often mistaken for Fischer's lovebird, which is slightly larger, with a blue rump.

clues.name: Lion
clues.fact: In Ngorongoro Crater, lions live largely on kills stolen from hyenas, but in Botswana's Chobe National Park the hyenas do the stealing.

clues.name: Plains Zebra
clues.fact: The largest wild zebra herd outside Africa roams San Simeon, California, descended from animals left behind when Hearst Castle's private zoo closed.

clues.name: Southern Giraffe
clues.fact: Also called the two-horned giraffe, it has rounded or blotched spots, some with star-like points, running all the way down to its hooves.

clues.name: Meves's Starling
clues.fact: It can look plain black in dull light, and its longer, strongly graduated tail sets it apart from Burchell's starling.

clues.name: Wahlberg’s Striped Skink
clues.fact: The Wahlberg in its name was Johan August Wahlberg, a Swedish naturalist, and this skink gives birth to live young.

clues.name: Bradfield's Hornbill
clues.fact: An uncommon bird of mopane woodland, it has white tips on its long tail and a long bill with no casque.

clues.name: African Buffalo
clues.fact: Herds decide where to eat or drink by 'voting', with females standing up before dusk to point in a particular direction.

clues.name: Common Hippopotamus
clues.fact: For an animal that spends most of the day in water, it may not swim at all, walking or bouncing along the bottom instead.

clues.name: Vervet Monkey
clues.fact: Leopards, martial eagles, rock pythons and baboons each get their own alarm call, which infants learn by observation alone.

clues.name: Nyala
clues.fact: Males and females look more different than in any other spiral-horned antelope, the males slate gray and horned, the females rusty brown and striped.

clues.name: Red-capped Robin-Chat
clues.fact: Hippopotamus droppings sometimes go into its nest, an open cup both parents build from dead leaves, moss, lichen and bark.

clues.name: Southern Crested Guineafowl
clues.fact: A courting male may run several meters to the hen to present her with a particular morsel.

clues.name: Spotted Hyena
clues.fact: The pitch of its famous laugh gives away a hyena's age, while the notes it uses signal its social rank.

clues.name: Common Ostrich
clues.fact: Its eyes are the largest of any land vertebrate, 50 millimetres across, which helps it spot predators at a great distance.

clues.name: Cape Sparrow
clues.fact: Also called the mossie, it appeared on South Africa's lowest-value coin from the 1923 farthing until the cent stopped being minted in 2002.

clues.name: Sociable Weaver
clues.fact: Its communal nest looks like a haystack in a tree and can house over 100 pairs, several generations at a time.

clues.name: Rough Thicktail Scorpion
clues.fact: Like nearly all thick-tailed scorpions, it makes a warning sound by rubbing its sting against the rough base of its tail.

clues.name: Karasburg Tree Skink
clues.fact: The Trachylepis in its scientific name means 'rough-scaled', since most Trachylepis skinks have faint ridges on smooth-looking back scales.

clues.name: Guttural Toad
clues.fact: After about 75 days as tadpoles, young toads can leave the ponds in such numbers that they carpet the ground.

clues.name: Redleg Orbweaver
clues.fact: Strong enough to snag the occasional bird or bat, its web is spun from yellow silk that shines like gold in sunlight.

clues.name: Tailless Tenrec
clues.fact: The first tropical mammal observed to hibernate, it can go up to nine months at a time without waking.

clues.name: Mascarene Paradise-Flycatcher
clues.fact: It lacks the long tail of many paradise flycatchers, so look instead for the male's black head, chestnut back and bright blue bill.

clues.name: Ornate Day Gecko
clues.fact: In 2014 five of these geckos were sent to space for a microgravity breeding test, and died after their heating system failed.

clues.name: Bojer's Skink
clues.fact: Invasive Asian house shrews helped drive its decline, and the Mauritian Wildlife Foundation has since eradicated them from its habitat.

clues.name: Oriental Magpie-Robin
clues.fact: Bangladesh's national bird, known there as the doyel, appears on a banknote and gives its name to Doel Square in Dhaka.

clues.name: Rhesus Macaque
clues.fact: In 1938 a Florida tour boat operator released some at Silver Springs to live on a river island, not realizing they're strong swimmers.

clues.name: Tiger
clues.fact: Besides roaring, tigers make a deer-like 'pok' sound, most often at kills, for reasons that are still unknown.

clues.name: Gharial
clues.fact: The pot-shaped knob on a male's snout, the ghara behind its name, lets him make a hiss that can be heard 75 meters away.

clues.name: Terai Sacred Langur
clues.fact: A leaf-eater of the sal forest canopy, it has also been seen feeding in orchards and crop fields outside Rajaji National Park.

clues.name: Indian Rhinoceros
clues.fact: When fighting, it inflicts wounds mostly with its lower incisors and uses its horn less often than African rhinos do.

clues.name: Asian Weaver Ant
clues.fact: To stitch leaves into a nest, workers wave larvae back and forth across the seams like living shuttles, making them release silk.

clues.name: Dusky Eagle-Owl
clues.fact: One of the world's least studied owls, it reuses stick nests of other large birds, in Haryana mostly those of woolly-necked storks.

clues.name: Spiny Orb-Weaver Spider
clues.fact: Like other spiny-backed orb-weavers, females are several times larger than the males, which lack the prominent spines and bright colors.

clues.name: Indian Pied Starling
clues.fact: The Sema Nagas won't eat this bird because they believe it's the reincarnation of a human.

clues.name: Indian Roofed Turtle
clues.fact: In October, just before the breeding season, males grow a small knob at the end of their thick tails and shed it in March.

clues.name: Grey-backed Shrike
clues.fact: Harsh zzert-zzert calls mark its territory, but its breeding song is subdued and musical, with several minutes of mimicked bird calls.

clues.name: Giant Golden Orbweaver
clues.fact: Females can be up to ten times the size of males and, unlike other golden orb-weavers, bury their eggs in a pit.

clues.name: Common Water Monitor
clues.fact: Its species name, salvator, means 'savior' in Latin, but in Thailand the lizard's name has long been a swearword.

clues.name: Forest Garden Lizard
clues.fact: Look for three separate small clusters of spines on each side of its head, one behind the brow and two above the eardrum.

clues.name: Northern Gray-bellied Squirrel
clues.fact: True to its name, its belly is usually gray, while its back is gray, yellowish-olive or reddish depending on subspecies and season.

clues.name: Variable Squirrel
clues.fact: Living up to the name variable squirrel, it can be whitish, blackish or reddish all over, depending on the subspecies.

clues.name: Northern Pig-tailed Macaque
clues.fact: Groups can top 150 monkeys, splitting into smaller parties to feed and coming back together to travel.

clues.name: Asian Honey Bee
clues.fact: In Vietnam, colonies have been found using animal dung and even human urine to defend their hives against hornet raids.

clues.name: Taiga Flycatcher
clues.fact: You can tell it from the red-breasted flycatcher by the female's blackish tail and the breeding male's orange-red, which stops at the throat.

clues.name: Black-crested Bulbul
clues.fact: Look for a black crested head with a yellow eye, and in central and eastern Thailand, a red throat as well.

clues.name: Black-striped Frog
clues.fact: Also called the sapgreen stream frog, it lives along gentle streams in evergreen forest, where its tadpoles grow up in the quiet stretches.

clues.name: Lanna Green Pitviper
clues.fact: Like every Asian palm pit viper, it has venom that mainly attacks the blood and is considered medically significant to humans.

clues.name: Common Mormon Swallowtail
clues.fact: Named in India with a nod to Mormon polygamy, it has three different forms of female, two of which mimic poisonous rose swallowtails.

clues.name: Common Sun Skink
clues.fact: First spotted in Taiwan in 1992, it has spread through the island's western lowlands but its poor cold tolerance keeps it below 500 meters.

clues.name: Asian Glossy Starling
clues.fact: Adults are glossy black and most have bright red eyes, while streaky juveniles have eyes of yellow, orange or pink.

clues.name: Rufous-legged Grasshopper
clues.fact: Wide black spots mark its slender hind thighs, and young hoppers pass through about five stages before they grow wings.

clues.name: Black-thighed Falconet
clues.fact: About the size of a sparrow, it's one of the smallest birds of prey and usually breeds in an old barbet nest hole.

clues.name: Malayan Crested Fireback
clues.fact: Look for white central tail feathers and red legs, which set it apart from the Bornean crested fireback it was once lumped with.

rounds.name: Bako National Park
rounds.official: Taman Negara Bako National Park, SK, MY

clues.name: Brahminy Kite
clues.fact: To the Iban of Sarawak's Upper Rajang, this kite is the war god Singalang Burung when he comes down to earth.

clues.name: Ornate Sunbird
clues.fact: Using grass, moss, lichens and spider webs, the female builds a hanging nest up to 60 cm long with a hooded side entrance.

clues.name: Common Parasol
clues.fact: Neurothemis, the first word of its scientific name, pairs the Greek for 'vein' with Themis, the goddess of divine law and order.

clues.name: Brown Marsh Frog
clues.fact: It's also called the Baram River frog, after its type locality on the Baram River in Sarawak.

clues.name: Blue-eyed Anglehead Lizard
clues.fact: Only males have the blue eyes in its name, while females have brown ones.

clues.name: Bornean Copper-cheeked Frog
clues.fact: Its tadpoles stand out, with dark markings and red gills on a light brown to yellow body, and they're presumably poisonous.

rounds.name: Danum Valley
rounds.official: Danum Valley Conservation Area, SA, MY

clues.name: Crimson Marsh Glider
clues.fact: Males are crimson with a violet tinge and even have crimson wing veins, while females are olive and reddish brown.

clues.name: Yellow-vented Bulbul
clues.fact: At home around people, it even nests in gardens, building a loose cup that looks untidy outside but is neatly lined with plant fibers.

clues.name: Dark-eared Tree Frog
clues.fact: Found even in some large cities, it lays its eggs in foam nests on leaves or twigs that hang over ponds and ditches.

clues.name: Bornean Keeled Pit Viper
clues.fact: Females can reach 96 cm, more than twice a male's maximum of 46 cm, and give birth to live young.

clues.name: Prevost's Squirrel
clues.fact: Durians are on its menu, and by carrying fruit far from the tree before dropping the seeds, it helps those plants survive.

clues.name: Maroon Leaf Monkey
clues.fact: It eats topsoil from termite mounds, which is high in calcium and magnesium, to keep its diet balanced.

clues.name: Chestnut Tiger
clues.fact: Its pupa is pale emerald green with golden-yellow spots, and eggs laid in September have produced adults the following April.

clues.name: Common Bluebottle
clues.fact: Its retinas have 15 types of color-detecting opsins, and its quick flight and rapid reactions make it difficult to catch.

clues.name: Light-vented Bulbul
clues.fact: A familiar bird of towns and urban parks, it may be Shanghai's third most common bird after tree sparrows and spotted doves.

clues.name: Pallas' Squirrel
clues.fact: It's been seen mobbing tree-climbing snakes, and females protecting their young are especially likely to join in.

clues.name: Taiwan Japalure
clues.fact: A sit-and-wait hunter that eats mostly ants, it's native to Taiwan but has turned up as an invasive species in Japan.

clues.name: Taiwan Common Toad
clues.fact: In one study, toads from a temperate area could breed all year, but subtropical ones bred only in the cooler months, September to March.

clues.name: Large-billed Crow
clues.fact: In Japan it's considered a pest, ripping open garbage bags and making off with wire coat hangers to build its nests.

clues.name: Indian Red Admiral
clues.fact: Its caterpillar feeds on nettles and ramie, then folds a leaf, ties the edges together with silk and pupates inside.

clues.name: Common Mapwing
clues.fact: Its domed eggs have a toothed lid like a cogwheel, which the caterpillar lifts to climb out, leaving the shell uneaten.

clues.name: Formosan Rock Macaque
clues.fact: Taiwan's only native primate apart from people, it screams when outsiders come near its troop.

clues.name: White-whiskered Laughingthrush
clues.fact: Found only in Taiwan's mountains, it's often seen in large groups and doesn't always shy away from people.

clues.name: Oriental Turtle-Dove
clues.fact: The Ainu traditionally hear its call as a saying: 'turtle dove ploughs, grandmother draws water, wife cooks, little master eats'.

clues.name: Oriental Magpie
clues.fact: Korean children were taught to toss a lost tooth onto the roof while singing to the magpie, which would bring a new one.

clues.name: Japanese Tree Frog
clues.fact: Males space out their calls so females can locate each one, a trick people have copied to design wireless networks with no central hub.

clues.name: Jeju Salamander
clues.fact: Jeju isn't its only home: it also lives on Chindo Island and at the southern tip of the Korean Peninsula.

clues.name: Sacred Kingfisher
clues.fact: The 'sacred' in its name comes from a 1782 claim that Polynesians revered it for haunting their marae and burial grounds.

clues.name: Australian Brushturkey
clues.fact: Goannas love its eggs, so they often end up with pecked tails from being chased ferociously off its nest mound.

clues.name: Eastern Saw-shelled Turtle
clues.fact: One of the few native Australian animals that successfully prey on poisonous cane toads, it shreds big ones with its front claws first.

clues.name: Southern Cassowary
clues.fact: Of 150 attacks on people in a 2003 study, three in four came from birds people had fed, and only one was fatal.

clues.name: Orange-footed Scrubfowl
clues.fact: Only the size of a chicken, it builds nest mounds of sand and leaf litter up to 4.5 meters tall and 9 meters across.

clues.name: orange pore fungus
clues.fact: Nicknamed the orange Ping-Pong bat for its shape, it's been in New Zealand since the 1950s but wasn't collected in mainland Australia until 2004.

clues.name: Australian Magpie
clues.fact: Australian magpies can recognise at least 100 different people and may be less likely to swoop the ones they've befriended.

clues.name: Laughing Kookaburra
clues.fact: Its laughing territorial call, often given by several birds at once, is widely used as a stock jungle sound effect.

clues.name: Asian Magpie Moth
clues.fact: This day-flying moth ranges from India all the way to Samoa, and its caterpillars have been recorded on Brassica plants.

clues.name: Koala
clues.fact: Its eucalyptus diet is low in nutrition and toxic enough to deter most other mammals, and it sleeps up to twenty hours a day.

clues.name: Wide-brand Grass-dart
clues.fact: Its caterpillars feed on Sorghum, Paspalum and Leersia, resting in a shelter made from blades of the plant joined with silk.

rounds.name: K'gari
rounds.official: K’gari (Fraser Island)  World Heritage Site, QL, AU

clues.name: White-faced Heron
clues.fact: It reached New Zealand on its own in the late 1940s, and it's the only heron recorded breeding in Tasmania.

clues.name: Rainbow Lorikeet
clues.fact: According to BirdLife Australia's annual census, it's the most commonly observed bird in Australia.

clues.name: Lace Monitor
clues.fact: Mitochondrial DNA shows its closest relative is the Komodo dragon, and the two lineages split more than 11 million years ago.

clues.name: Carpet Python
clues.fact: After laying 10 to 50 eggs, the female coils around them, warming them with heat from her own muscle contractions.

clues.name: Daemel's Spiny Ant
clues.fact: Like other Polyrhachis ants, it has no stinger and sprays formic acid instead, often while biting, which makes the acid more effective.

clues.name: Dune Ringtail
clues.fact: Its species name, minjerriba, is the Aboriginal name for North Stradbroke Island, where this damselfly of acidic dune lakes was first recorded.

clues.name: Sacred Kingfisher
clues.fact: The 'sacred' in its name comes from a 1782 claim that Polynesians revered it for haunting their marae and burial grounds.

clues.name: three spot skipper
clues.fact: The caterpillars eat four kinds of Lepidosperma as well as Phlebocarya ciliata, and adults have a wingspan of about 35 millimeters.

clues.name: Superb Fairywren
clues.fact: Males pluck yellow petals and show them to females, sometimes in other territories and even outside the breeding season.

clues.name: Bogong Moth
clues.fact: Flying by night to the Australian Alps, it may navigate by both the stars and Earth's magnetic field, researchers suggested in 2025.

clues.name: Eastern Water Skink
clues.fact: Gaps in its range line up with places where the Great Escarpment is absent, suggesting low ground and dry forest act as barriers.

clues.name: Mountain Clubmoss
clues.fact: Upright and conifer-like, this clubmoss grows up to 10 cm tall and can look bright orange in cold conditions.

clues.name: Wire Rush
clues.fact: Its scientific name translates as 'small tangle-foot', and its stems stand upright when short but lie along the ground once tall.

clues.name: Red-necked Wallaby
clues.fact: Courtship starts with the female licking the male's neck, and the pair even spar briefly, standing upright like two males, before mating.

clues.name: Australian Wood Duck
clues.fact: It nests in tree hollows, and when it's time to leave, the mother flies down and the ducklings leap to the ground after her.

clues.name: Yellow-bellied Water Skink
clues.fact: Look for it basking on waterside logs and rocks, as it prefers rocky places near creeks, rivers, bogs and swamps.

clues.name: Chameleon Grasshopper
clues.fact: Most grasshoppers stay passive or chirp to settle disputes, but this one is known among entomologists for frequent, escalated physical fights.

clues.name: Silver Gull
clues.fact: Australia's most common gull, it's known to pester people for chips and to steal food left unattended.

clues.name: Australian Ibis
clues.fact: Ibises in several regions have learned to eat cane toads by flicking them until they release their toxin, then washing them in water.

clues.name: Crimson Rosella
clues.fact: In the breeding season, females often raid other rosellas' nests and destroy the eggs, the most common reason an egg fails to hatch.

clues.name: Painted Trilling Frog
clues.fact: When threatened, it sometimes rears up on all its legs and inflates its body to look bigger to predators.

clues.name: Western Grey Kangaroo
clues.fact: Mature males have a distinctive curry-like smell, which earned the species its nickname, 'stinker'.

clues.name: Tammar Wallaby
clues.fact: It can survive by drinking seawater, which lets it live on several islands that have no fresh water.

clues.name: Little Pied Cormorant
clues.fact: In New Zealand the mostly black, white-throated form wins out, and even in Northland only about one in four birds is pied.

clues.name: Zebra Finch
clues.fact: More than half the birds in one experiment survived 513 days without being given any water to drink.

clues.name: Central Netted Dragon
clues.fact: About a quarter of its wild diet is plants, like hogweed and daisy flowers, making it one of Australia's most herbivorous desert lizards.

clues.name: Western Bowerbird
clues.fact: Males decorate their bowers with green and white objects like berries, shells and bones, and sometimes glass and gun casings.

clues.name: Inland Hooded Snake
clues.fact: A solid glossy black hood covers the top of its head and nape, set against a brick-red back and white belly.

clues.name: Centralian Earless Dragon
clues.fact: Tympanocryptis, the first part of its scientific name, means 'hidden ear', and centralis refers to its central Australian range.

clues.name: Bluespot Butterflyfish
clues.fact: Juveniles have been recorded working as cleaner fish, picking parasites off other fish, while adults feed mostly on coral polyps.

clues.name: Pied Currawong
clues.fact: Flocks seem to play, with one bird perching atop a tall tree or spire while others swoop and dive trying to knock it off.

clues.name: Tiger Spider
clues.fact: This orb weaver packs uneaten prey into a storage band near its web's hub and eats from it when catches are poor.

clues.name: Festive Nudibranch
clues.fact: Look for raised pink spots on a white body and a broken yellow line running around the edge of its mantle.

rounds.name: Tongariro National Park
rounds.official: Tongariro National Park World Heritage Site, NZ

clues.name: Biddy-biddy
clues.fact: Each fruit carries four barbed spines, red when ripe, that hitch rides on wool, feathers and clothing.

clues.name: alpine coral-fern
clues.fact: Turn a frond over to find deep, densely hairy pouches under the leaflets, which leave Gleichenia dicarpa as its only lookalike.

clues.name: Australian Pug Moth
clues.fact: Its caterpillars eat flowers, acacia blossoms in Australia and gorse in New Zealand, where it arrived on its own in 1960.

clues.name: New Zealand Fantail
clues.fact: Not shy around people, it often flits within a few meters of them to catch insects stirred up by their walking or digging.

clues.name: North Island Robin
clues.fact: Mates raid each other's food caches, and a robin is less likely to stash food while its partner is around.

clues.name: Sigaus piliferus
clues.fact: Its longer-legged shrubland form and its alpine form, probably separated during the last ice age, now meet among the central North Island volcanoes.

clues.name: Little Pied Cormorant
clues.fact: In New Zealand the mostly black, white-throated form wins out, and even in Northland only about one in four birds is pied.

clues.name: Mānuka
clues.fact: The easiest way to tell it from kānuka is to feel the leaves: mānuka's are prickly, while kānuka's are soft.

clues.name: New Zealand Pigeon
clues.fact: After eating, it often suns itself, which can ferment the fruit in its crop and leave the bird drunk.

clues.name: Tomtit
clues.fact: Tomtits on the Snares Islands are entirely black and weigh about 20 grams, almost twice as much as birds on the main islands.

clues.name: Alpine Treasure Owlet
clues.fact: Nobody has confirmed what its caterpillars eat in the wild, and ones raised from eggs in captivity didn't make it to adulthood.
